gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the two 6,000 W units (Nature's Generator L6000, Anker SOLIX F3800 Plus) cap their 120/240 V output at 25 A while the 7,200 W units are 30 A-class, that only the EcoFlow TITAN 5000 Plus is claimed by its maker to put up to 5 kW on one 120 V leg, or which transfer switch, charging cable and expansion battery the L6000 takes.
standout_why: Compared against solarwaypoint.com (cited: outlet counts only, no outlet types, amp limits or transfer gear beyond one Smart Home Panel 2 mention), holdbackup.com (cited: has transfer-switch and expansion-battery pairings for Jackery 5000 Plus, F3800 Plus and DELTA Pro Ultra and '6,000 W total on the L14-30R', but no amp cap and no L6000, TITAN or Pecron), thewattguide.com (has Jackery's 30 A 240 V outlets, two 3,600 W 120 V banks and the 30 A inlet arithmetic), theoutageplan.com (panel pairings for four models) and powerbencher.com (older F3800 only). None covers the L6000 at all, none gives the 25 A cap on either 6,000 W unit, and none gives the TITAN 5000 Plus 5 kW-per-leg claim or its Smart Home Panel 10 requirement. Pairings for Jackery, Anker and DELTA Pro Ultra are already on holdbackup, so that part is not new.
decides: It confirms rather than overturns the pick. A 5,000 W load at 240 V draws 20.8 A, so it fits every candidate, but the 25 A units (L6000, F3800 Plus) leave about 1,000 W for anything else on at the same time, against about 2,200 W on a 7,200 W unit. A 5,000 W load at 120 V (41.7 A) fits no single 120 V outlet I could source on any candidate; only EcoFlow claims 5 kW on one 120 V leg, for the TITAN 5000 Plus 'in a supported configuration'. So the L6000 is honest as the in-stock pick for a 5,000 W 240 V load (well pump, dryer through a transfer switch) with its 25 A ceiling stated in the row; a shopper who needs headroom above 5,000 W or a heavy single-leg 120 V load is steered to a 7,200 W unit. The L6000 row should also name its own accessories: 30 A or 50 A transfer switch (manual or automatic), the $119.99 14-50 Super Charging Cable for 3,600 W charging, and the $1,499.99 Power Pod.

findings.label: Amp limit behind the 6,000 W rating
findings.value: 6,000 W = 120/240 V at 25 A from one unit; 12,000 W = 120/240 V at 50 A from two units joined by the L6000 Combiner Cable
findings.note: Maker's listing text read through storecheck search. Arithmetic: 5,000 W / 240 V = 20.8 A, leaving 4.2 A (about 1,000 W) under the 25 A cap.

findings.label: Combiner cable for two units
findings.value: $199.99; compatibility chart lists the L6000 only ('Full support')
findings.note: Listed as available. No other Nature's Generator model appears in the chart.

findings.label: 3,600 W charging: cable and outlet required
findings.value: Lithium 6ft Super Charging Cable, $119.99, requires a NEMA 14-50R 240 V outlet; charges the L6000 to 80% in about 1.2 hours; passes through up to 6,000 W (120/240 V) as a UPS while charging
findings.source_title: Nature's Generator Lithium 6ft Super Charging Cable
findings.note: Compatibility chart: L6000, Powerhouse 7200 Gen 2, MyGrid 10K Gen 1 and Gen 2. The L6000 listing gives AC charging as '1,800W or 3,600W'; the 1.2-hour figure belongs to this separately sold cable.

findings.label: Transfer switch pairing
findings.value: Maker sells the L6000 bundled with a choice of 30 A or 50 A transfer switch, manual or automatic; Auto-Start ECO Mode (automatic restore on grid loss) works only when paired with an automatic transfer switch
findings.source_title: Nature's Generator L6000 Whole Home Backup
findings.note: Listing returned $2,649.99, available; I could not read which switch variant that price belongs to (the product page returned HTTP 429). One L6000 supplies 25 A, so a 50 A switch is fed at half its rating by a single unit (my arithmetic from the combiner-cable page, not a maker statement).

findings.label: Expansion battery
findings.value: L6000 Power Pod, $1,499.99: adds 3,840 Wh, 1,200 W of charging and 100 W DC output; 'specifically engineered to work with the Lithium 6000'
findings.note: Plug-in, no installer needed per the listing. UL 2743. The L3600 has its own separate Power Pod (named in the maker's cover and cart charts).

findings.label: Price and stock, battery unit alone
findings.source_title: Nature's Generator L6000 Expandable Power Station
findings.note: Read through storecheck search. The sale end date was not on the text returned.

findings.label: 240 V outlet rating
findings.value: NEMA L14-30R: 120 V/240 V, 25 A max, 6,000 W max; total AC output 6,000 W max
findings.source_title: F3800 Plus Portable Power Station - Anker SOLIX US
findings.note: A 30 A receptacle limited to 25 A by the inverter. Same 1,000 W of headroom over a 5,000 W 240 V load as the L6000.

findings.label: 120 V outlet rating
findings.value: AC Output 1 and 2: 120 V, 20 A max, 2,400 W max each; the left three 5-20R ports have UPS
findings.source_title: F3800 Plus Portable Power Station - Anker SOLIX US
findings.note: A single 5,000 W 120 V appliance (41.7 A) does not fit a 20 A outlet. The page lists a TT-30R but gave no amp or watt rating in the text returned.

findings.label: Generator bypass exclusion
findings.value: Anker SOLIX Generator Adapter required; bypass supports a single F3800 Plus unit only
findings.source_title: F3800 Plus Portable Power Station - Anker SOLIX US
findings.note: Whole-home backup and automatic backup features are footnoted 'Home Power Panel required'. Price and stock did not appear in the text returned.

findings.label: Output by source and per 120 V leg
findings.value: 7.2 kW from the battery alone at 120/240 V; up to 10 kW only while compatible solar is connected and producing; X-Boost 2.0: up to 5 kW on either 120 V leg 'in a supported configuration', with the 7.2 kW battery total still applying
findings.source_title: What Can EcoFlow TITAN Power? Output & Runtime Guide
findings.note: EcoFlow says the per-leg X-Boost 2.0 figure is not listed for the standard TITAN 5000. EcoFlow also notes each outlet, breaker and cable has its own rating, which may be lower.

findings.label: Home panel required for automatic switchover
findings.value: Smart Home Panel 10, installed by a qualified electrician; on the Plus it backs up to 10 selected circuits with 20 ms switchover
findings.source_title: What Can EcoFlow TITAN Power? Output & Runtime Guide
findings.note: Generator-plus-battery operation on the Plus needs EcoFlow's 'approved FlowMaster configuration', which is separate from plain AC charging.

findings.label: Excluded from the 5,000 W line
findings.value: 4 kW at 120 V; EcoFlow says it 'is not designed for 240V appliances like central AC, a well pump, or an electric dryer'
findings.source_title: What Can EcoFlow TITAN Power? Output & Runtime Guide
findings.note: Three TITAN variants share the 5 kWh name; only the 5000 and 5000 Plus are 7.2 kW 120/240 V. ChatGPT's answer told shoppers to 'verify the exact TITAN variant' without saying this.

findings.label: Accessory pairings stated by the maker
findings.value: Smart Home Panel 2: 12 circuits, 20 ms switchover; generator charging requires the AC Generator Charging Adapter (generator support up to 12 kW); EV charging up to 7.2 kW via the EV X-Stream Adapter; base system 6 kWh / 7.2 kW
findings.note: Footnote: a soft-starter may be needed if an air conditioner's LRA is not within 120 A. The page showed a quote form, with no price or stock status.

findings.label: Accessories Jackery marks as compatible
findings.value: Smart Transfer Switch; Manual Transfer Switch (240V); Battery Pack 5000 Plus; Power Input/Output Cable. A different Manual Transfer Switch is listed for the HomePower 3600 Pro Max, not the 5000 Plus
findings.note: Jackery sells two manual transfer switches; only the 240 V one is tagged for the 5000 Plus. The same page lists the Double Kit as 10,080 Wh / 14,400 W.
